title: Lose, and Lose, and Lose, and Win
gist: Ben Landau-Taylor argues insurgent parties win only after years of losing while building cadre and doctrine, then fill the vacuum when a mainstream party collapses (Bolsheviks, Republicans, DSA); Brazil's Mission Party is positioned to wait for such a collapse.

insights.claim: Successful insurgent parties follow a pattern: a long gatekept period building infrastructure, cadre and doctrine, then a sharp collapse of a mainstream segment which they rapidly fill with ready organizers, ideology and mobilization.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: A reusable model for spotting which political movements are positioned to inherit a collapsing establishment.
insights.quote: They go through a long period of wandering in the wilderness

insights.claim: The collapse's timing cannot be predicted because it depends on individuals; the vacuum goes to whoever has the best mix of pre-existing infrastructure, skill at navigating intrigue and will to take risks, whether an organized vanguard or an opportunist.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Do not trade the timing of regime collapse; watch which organizations are prepared.
insights.locator: What does this mean for an insurgent party's strategy?

insights.claim: Collapses could have been delayed by contingencies, such as Biden's health holding, Asquith and Lloyd George restraining their rivalry, or Franklin Pierce not backing the Kansas-Nebraska Act.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Individual-level contingencies drive timing, so tail risks on political order are fat.
insights.locator: What does this mean for an insurgent party's strategy?

insights.claim: Russian Marxists formed in 1883, played a minor role in 1905, and by 1917 Lenin's Bolsheviks maneuvered to the head of rioters and mutineers when the exhausted Tsarist regime collapsed.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Canonical example of decades of cadre-building paying off at a collapse.

insights.claim: In the US, the Liberty Party (1841) and Free Soil Party (1848) fed into the new Republican Party after the Whig Party shattered over the Kansas-Nebraska Act in 1854.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Shows small single-issue insurgents becoming the governing party after a major party breaks.
insights.locator: In America, the most important case

insights.claim: Other examples include the Young Turks, British Labour after the Liberal collapse, the Nazi Party as Weimar disintegrated, and de Gaulle's Fifth Republic.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Pattern is recurrent across regimes and eras.

insights.claim: The Democratic machine is being supplanted by a DSA-originated machine and ideology, with DSA having quintupled membership by 2017, sent first members to Congress in 2018, and much of its platform now adopted by mainstream Democrats, with Zohran Mamdani's NYC mayoral win as its signature success.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Expect progressive-left policy positions to anchor Democratic platforms, including on NYC economics and taxes.

insights.claim: The Republican establishment collapsed by 2016 with no organized insurgent right-wing faction ready, so Trump personally filled the vacuum without cadre, making his first term ineffective and his second coalition only loosely cohesive.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: MAGA lacks ideological cohesion and cadre depth, a durability risk for its policy agenda.
insights.locator: A few years before the old liberal Democratic Party collapsed

insights.claim: In Brazil's election Renan Santos of the Mission Party placed fourth with 2.6 million votes (2.2%) after twelve years of campaigning and kept its single federal legislative seat; the run-off is between 80-year-old Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: Brazil's runoff features two weak establishment candidates; an outsider could benefit if machines fail.
insights.quote: lose, and lose, and lose, and win

insights.claim: The Mission Party grew from mass protests against corruption under Dilma Rousseff, institutionalized the energy, and continues building cadre, doctrine and mass mobilization for a future opportunity.
insights.speaker: Ben Landau-Taylor
insights.so_what: A long-horizon outsider bet on Brazilian political realignment.
